# Rahul Mitra (rahul-mitra.com)

> Multidisciplinary engineer in Singapore: software systems, AI engineering, operations research, 3D computer vision, solution architecture, and cybersecurity. NUS Industrial Systems Engineering (Second Major in Computer Science, Minor in Mathematics).

## Machine-readable access
- MCP server (Streamable HTTP): https://rahul-mitra.com/api/mcp
  Tools (open, no auth): get_profile, list_experience, list_projects, get_project, list_resumes, get_resume, get_resume_guide, list_resume_blocks, build_resume, check_resume, export_profile, build_tailored_resume
  Tools (Rahul only, Authorization: Bearer): get_job_preferences, set_job_preferences, create_application, update_application, list_applications
- JSON export of the same data, résumés included as Markdown: https://rahul-mitra.com/api/portfolio
- Résumé builder: call get_resume_guide, then list_resume_blocks, then build_resume to compose a Harvard-style résumé targeted at a specific role. Content is selected from Rahul's approved blocks; bullet text cannot be supplied, so nothing on a generated résumé is invented.
- Alternative phrasings: some bullets carry more than one approved wording of the same fact, shown on list_resume_blocks with each one's opening verb, line cost and whether it holds a measurement. A build selects one by id. Nothing here lets a caller supply text: the choice is between Rahul's own sentences.
- Résumé checker: build_resume returns a check report, and check_resume runs the same check on any ready-made résumé. It is deterministic and rule-based, naming repeated opening verbs, repeated sentence frames, hedging words, bullets with no measurable outcome and bullets over the line budget, each against the block ids it found them on. It reports counts rather than a score, and it never rewrites text.
- Profile export: export_profile returns cv.md, profile.yml and article-digest.md in career-ops shape, projected at call time from the same data every other tool serves rather than hand-authored, so nothing in them is invented or separately maintained. article-digest.md and profile.yml's proof points are a SELECTED set of spotlight projects, each with its own outcome and anchor — a few are held back from them as a presentation choice, and cv.md and list_projects remain complete. A project absent from the digest is therefore not a subject to avoid: cv.md is the authority on Rahul's experience and every bullet in it is approved for employer-facing use, including where it describes work that is also a portfolio project. The keys that tooling expects but this repository cannot attest (phone, compensation, notice period) are omitted and named in `gaps` rather than guessed — a sync should preserve whatever it holds locally at those keys. The availability block and target roles come from the token-gated preferences, so an anonymous caller gets the committed defaults and `preferences_source` says which of the two was used.
- Job search: preferences and the application tracker are Rahul's own and token-gated; an unauthenticated caller gets a refusal, not data. build_tailored_resume never fetches a job-description URL and never lets job-description text reach a document: the posting chooses among Rahul's own blocks and his attested vocabulary (the resume keyword rows plus his skills lines) and contributes no words of its own; the coverage report it returns is drawn from that same vocabulary, so it names his terms and never quotes the posting. The jd_hash that identifies a posting is derived from the normalized URL when one is given and from the text only otherwise, so an edited or re-scraped posting stays one row in the tracker.
- Site: https://rahul-mitra.com/
